comments.text:
I’m a new mother. I live in SC. There is currently an outbreak of measles here. 2 weeks ago at my son’s two month appointment, his pediatrician said “Mrs. I know you’ve made up your mind but I really want to provide some additional education on vaccinations”. My eyes widened and I said “made up my mind for what? He’s getting vaccinated period”. His pediatrician made the biggest sigh and said “Oh thank God. I don’t know why the nurse charted against it but we’ll get them prepped”. The pediatrician came back in and asked if I had relayed any information that I was potentially against vaccination. I vehemently denied this. They stated the nurse had stated she “assumed since he had yet to have his shots, the parent was against them”. I was so shook. I am 26 years old and for this nurse to just make an assumption without asking me, it bothered me terribly. He ended up getting his shots and I have not seen that nurse since we have been back for 1 follow up. I just can’t help but imagine if I was uneducated or had my doctor just went with the flow… Especially, during my postpartum period when forgetfulness and confusion is a given. My baby would be at risk. I’m so grateful for the healthcare professionals that speak up - The ones who ask questions and double check. The ones who take the time to educate even though it often falls on deaf ears. It is so important.

EDIT/UPDATE 
My son went back to the pediatrician for his 4 month follow (including secondary vaccination dosages). I asked about the nurse who my initial comment referenced. The on-site phlebotomist notified me that they let her go. I told her I felt extremely bad and felt guilty. Even though she made what I assume was a mistake, I didn’t want her to lose her livelihood. Shockingly, the phlebotomist informed that the incident with my son was the 5th instance of “vaccination refusal” that was “incorrectly” charted by this specific nurse. The practice had to release her after 2 of the 5 children (infants) effected had missed the window for their first immunizations. Solely because the nurse charted refusals and the parents had assumed their vaccinations would be presented at the right time. Like me, they were new parents and were not well informed so they trusted the healthcare professionals. Obviously, I am not privy to certain information like age, names, etc. due to HIPPA but the phlebotomist made it clear that I was not the only parent, and it appeared to be intentional misinformation charted by the nurse. I found the revelation so disturbing that I wanted to update my comment.

This comment will probably be buried here since this episode was two months ago, but I wanted to give a huge thank you for this podcast. When Dr Beachgem started talking about her breast cancer scare I felt a twinge in my breast and did a self exam. I caught a mass while watching this episode and am now going through chemo having caught my breast cancer in stage 2. I wanted to give some additional info to anybody who is in the same position as me. My cancer is lobular, it hides pretty well from mamograms and can't always be caught on self exams until it grows significantly. In addition to self exams for masses, bend over and examine your nipple position. Watch out for a nipple puckering when you're bent over. I didn't realize this was a sign and I might have caught it sooner if I had included this in my exam. Skin texture and nipple signs I've never really been trained to do and it would have helped in my case.

Thank you.
